varieties.name: Overberg
varieties.traits: Highest mean yield in the short-duration cereal trial (6.98 t DM/ha), but among the LATEST to reach silage harvest (166 days after planting) and lowest seed-head uniformity (only 50% seed heads, high variability) — better suited to grazing or hay than silage
varieties.note: Directly sources and extends the existing crop-catalog.ts 'daysToHarvest: 166' figure and comment, which this pass confirms comes from a KZN DARD Cedara forage-cereal trial rather than a food-oat context. Zones are this pass's inference from the trial location (KZN Midlands, Cedara) plus general applicability to the wider cold summer-rain interior; the source does not itself name zones.

evidence.quote: The highest mean yield in the short-duration trial was produced by Overberg oats at 6.98 tons DM ha-1
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

evidence.quote: the cultivars that had the latest silage harvest were Elisabet oats, Overberg oats and Estero 1430 red oat (166 days after planting).
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

evidence.quote: Overberg oats, with only 50% seed heads and high variability, may be less desirable for silage and probably more suited to grazing or hay.
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

varieties.name: Elisabet
varieties.traits: One of the three latest-maturing cultivars in the short-duration trial (166 days after planting)

evidence.quote: the cultivars that had the latest silage harvest were Elisabet oats, Overberg oats and Estero 1430 red oat (166 days after planting).
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

varieties.name: Estero 1430
varieties.traits: Red oat (Avena byzantina); one of the three latest-maturing cultivars in the short-duration trial (166 days after planting)
varieties.note: This is a red oat (A. byzantina), not the white oat (A. sativa) type used for Overberg/Elisabet — distinguished in the source. Same trial/zone inference as Overberg.

evidence.quote: the cultivars that had the latest silage harvest were Elisabet oats, Overberg oats and Estero 1430 red oat (166 days after planting).
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

varieties.name: Saddle
varieties.traits: White oat; among the quickest to establish in the medium/long-duration grazing trial (2.67 t DM/ha in the first cut)
varieties.note: From the separate medium/long-duration (repeated grazing) trial at the same Cedara site.

evidence.quote: Saddle oats, Moby barley and Saia black oats, with yields of 2.67, 2.64 and 2.63 tons DM ha-1, respectively, are considered quick to establish
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

varieties.name: Saia
varieties.traits: Black oat (Avena strigosa); among the quickest to establish in the medium/long-duration grazing trial (2.63 t DM/ha in the first cut)

evidence.quote: Saddle oats, Moby barley and Saia black oats, with yields of 2.67, 2.64 and 2.63 tons DM ha-1, respectively, are considered quick to establish
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

midlands-mistbelt.text: Directly sourced: this is where the Cedara trial ran. Short-duration cultivars (e.g. Overberg, Elisabet, Estero 1430) sown end Feb/March give autumn/early-winter grazing or an autumn silage cut; sowing later in autumn shifts grazing to early/mid-winter.

evidence.quote: Short duration cultivars are usually quick to establish and, if planted in early autumn (end of Feb/March), will provide grazing in late autumn/early winter.
evidence.doc: Short, medium and long duration cereals for cover crops and winter forage, KZN DARD Research & Technology Bulletin 2020/21-09

highveld.text: Extrapolated from the same Cedara trial to the wider cold summer-rain interior for the March-May cover-crop window already used in crop-catalog.ts — not independently confirmed for the highveld itself.

gaps: All cultivar data comes from a single KZN Midlands (Cedara) trial; no independent source confirms these specific cultivars' performance in the highveld, lowveld-bushveld, subtropical-coast, western-cape, southern-cape, karoo-arid or high-mountain zones.

The bulletin is about forage/cover-crop oats (matching this catalog entry's 'winter cover crop' framing), not grain oats for human consumption — if a food-oat use is ever added to the catalog, none of this evidence would carry over.
Medium/long-duration trial yields (Saddle, Saia, Moby barley) are given only for the first cut, not a full-season total, so a full-season yield-per-cultivar figure is a gap.
